technical_decisions: The cost is already in the Lab; it is missing from one frame only. XMage's priority() builds every option through abilityMetadata -> enrichAbilityCostFacts, and the announce_x frame raised inside that same action carries no cost at all. Remembering the chosen priority option's reported cost per seat bridges the hop with no bridge, protocol or pin change.

X is EXCLUDED from mana_cost_*: XMage holds {X} as a VariableManaCost whose own cost Mana is empty (cost = new Mana()) and whose value is fixed only after the announce (AbilityImpl.handleManaXCosts announces before expanding the cost). So the sum of the seven mana_cost_* components is the non-X mana value, which for {X}{1}{B} is 2. Corroborated by the repo's own JVM test XmageCausalStackMechanicsTest, where Sagu Mauler's {3} morph offer reads mana_cost_generic == 3 with green/blue 0 -- mana_cost_generic counts generic symbols only.

SUPERSEDED at 92195cb8: the bridge publishes no X count, so it used to be assumed to be 1. The engine's own prompt carries it instead: VariableManaCost.getText() prints each symbol separately, '{X}{X}' for {X}{X} and never '2{X}', so the X count is read off the prompt whenever no frame states one. {X}{X} now budgets as two symbols over what the rest of the cost leaves.

Mana budgeting is gated on mana_x_prompt_symbols matching the engine's WHOLE prompt: 'Announce the value for ' followed by one or more '{X}' and nothing else. Player.announceX serves BOTH handleManaXCosts (VariableManaCost.getText()) and the non-mana VariableCostImpl.announce with isManaPay == false, which prints 'Announce the value for {X} (' + actionText + ')' -- a '{X}' token followed by more text. Searching the prompt for a '{X}' token classified that non-mana X as a mana X; matching the whole prompt does not. The same whole-prompt match supplies the X count. This gate also keeps the synthetic WS229 announce_x frames (prompt 'announce_x') on their full domain, so no WS229 assertion was relaxed.
X announcement is CR 601.2b with 107.3a; the earlier record cited 107.3b, which is not the announcement rule. The same correction is in _option_non_x_mana_value and mana_x_prompt_symbols.

The ceiling is (budget - non_x) // x_symbols, clamped at 0: the rest of the cost is paid out of the same visible mana, and several X symbols share what is left. The previous budget // symbols - non_x subtracted the whole rest of the cost from each symbol's share.

REPLAY NOTE: a seeded mana-X decision now draws from a narrower band than the same seed drew from before this repair, so an older seeded record containing a mana X does NOT replay identically against this head. Every seeded record without a mana X is unaffected: the hint is gated on the engine's mana prompt and on decision_class == 'announce_x'.

Bounded fallback when nothing is readable: non-X cost 0 over the prompt's own symbol count, i.e. the whole visible budget for the ordinary single-X cost. Still far below 2147483647 and only ever lower than the domain allows, so the authoritative domain stays the sole validation target.

A remembered cost is TAKEN, not copied. One cost is announced once, so a second announce_x naming the same source before that seat's next priority decision falls back to the budget instead of answering twice from the same cost. The take happens only after the prompt gate, so a non-mana announce never consumes a mana cost it is not the use of.

A cost stated directly on the announce frame wins over the remembered one, so an engine statement is never overridden by an older one. A frame that states only half a cost (a non-X value with no count) stays unusable as it was: the prompt count is not filled into a statement the engine left incomplete, so the pre-existing symbols-absent control still falls back to the budget.

The memory is keyed on the engine's own source_object_id for EQUALITY only; it never orders, ranks or counts anything, so it cannot make same-seed fresh-process twins diverge. Last selection only, per seat, dropped on that seat's next priority decision or by the announce that uses it.
